Plot an evoked current trace

Source: R/Plot-data.R
plot_evoked_current_trace.Rd

This function allows you to generate an evoked current trace (averaged) from an .abf file, such as the representative traces seen above summary plots plot_summary_current_data(). Follow these steps:

Usage

plot_evoked_current_trace(
  data,
  plot_colour = "#000000",
  filename = "Cell-A-baseline-trace",
  include_scale_bar = "yes",
  include_scale_bar_label = "no",
  scale_bar_label_size = 4,
  trace_annotation = "",
  trace_annotation_x_position = 0.57,
  trace_annotation_y_position = 6,
  geom_text_family = "",
  geom_text_colour = "#000000",
  geom_text_size = 9,
  plot_episode = "epi1",
  geom_text_fontface = "bold",
  trace_thickness = 2,
  scale_bar_x_start = 0.6,
  scale_bar_x_length = 0.02,
  scale_bar_y_length = 50,
  scale_bar_y_start = -75,
  k_value = 100,
  scale_bar_linewidth = 0.75,
  scale_bar_label_y_nudge = 1.5,
  plot_x_min = 0.57,
  plot_x_max = 0.61,
  plot_y_min = -100,
  plot_y_max = 10,
  save_plot_png = "no",
  ggplot_theme = patchclampplotteR_theme()
)

Arguments

data

A dataframe containing at least these columns: time, episode, current, voltage, time_sec. An easy way to obtain this is by importing a raw .abf file through the import_ABF_file() function.

plot_colour

A character value naming the colour of the plot.

filename

A character value used for the filename when saving the ggplot object as a .png.

include_scale_bar

A character value that determines if a scale bar will be added to the plot. Allowed values are "yes" and "no".

include_scale_bar_label

A character value ("yes" or "no") describing whether to include text labels on the scale bar. If "yes", the text annotation values will be pulled from scale_bar_x_length and scale_bar_y_length.

scale_bar_label_size

A numeric value describing the size of the scale bar annotation text. Defaults to 4.

trace_annotation

A character value (e.g. "Baseline") that will be added as text on the plot. Useful for labelling traces for publications and presentations. Defaults to "" for blank.

trace_annotation_x_position

A numeric value for the location of the trace_annotation on the x-axis.

trace_annotation_y_position

A numeric value for the location of the trace_annotation on the y-axis.

geom_text_family

A character value describing the font family used for the scale bar annotations. Defaults to "" (empty, will use default system font), but can be replaced with a named font. Use a package like extrafont to load system fonts into R.

geom_text_colour

A character value describing the colour of the trace_annotation text. Defaults to "#000000", but you can match it to plot_colour for consistency.

geom_text_size

A numeric value describing the size of the trace_annotation text. Defaults to 5.

plot_episode

A character value describing the sweep (e.g. epi1) that will be used for the plot.

geom_text_fontface

A character value ("plain", "bold", "italic", "bold.italic"), used to describe the label defined in text_annotation. Defaults to "bold".

trace_thickness

A numeric value describing the thickness of the trace line. Defaults to 0.8.

scale_bar_x_start

A numeric value (in seconds) describing the x-axis position of the scale bar.

scale_bar_x_length

A numeric value describing the horizontal span (in seconds) of the scale bar. This will automatically be converted and displayed in milliseconds (default is 0.02 = 20 ms).

scale_bar_y_length

A numeric value describing the vertical span (in pA) of the scale bar (default is 50 pA).

scale_bar_y_start

A numeric value describing the y-axis position (in pA) of the scale bar.

k_value

Used define the k value used for smoothing in the GAM model. You can think of this as the number of nodes used in the model. Choose a higher value for a more detailed trace, and a lower number for a more smooth curve. Be careful not to distort the current trace by making this too smooth!

scale_bar_linewidth

A numeric value describing the thickness of the scalebar line (default is 0.75).

scale_bar_label_y_nudge

An optional numeric value that will add additional padding between the scale bar x-axis label and the scale bar. Defaults to 1.5.

plot_x_min

A numeric value describing the minimum value on the x-axis (in seconds). Defaults to 0.57.

plot_x_max

A numeric value describing the maximum value on the x-axis (in seconds). Defaults to 0.61.

plot_y_min

A numeric value describing the minimum value on the y-axis (in pA). Defaults to -100. !!Warning!! Be sure to check your raw current amplitudes and adjust this to avoid cutting off data!!

plot_y_max

A numeric value describing the maximum value on the y-axis (in pA). Defaults to 10. !!Warning!! Be sure to check your raw current amplitudes and adjust this to avoid cutting off data!!

save_plot_png

A character ("yes" or "no"). If "yes", the plot will be saved as a .png using ggsave(). The filepath depends on the current type, but they will all go in subfolders below Figures/ in your project directory.

ggplot_theme

The name of a ggplot theme or your custom theme. This will be added as a layer to a ggplot object. The default is patchclampplotteR_theme(), but other valid entries include theme_bw(), theme_classic() or the name of a custom ggplot theme stored as an object.

Value

A ggplot object. If save_plot_png is defined as "yes", it will also generate a .png file in the folder Figures/Representative-Traces relative to the project directory, with the filename characters included in the filename.

Details

  1. Open a recording file in Clampfit, and select the traces you would like to average (e.g. 60 sweeps from the baseline).

  2. Click on Analyze -> Average Traces and ensure that Display resultant trace only is checked. In Select, choose All visible traces.

  3. The .abf file should now have only one sweep.

  4. Surround a flat region of the trace with cursors 1 and 2, and the stimulus artifact with cursors 3 and 4.

  5. Flatten the stimulus artifacts by clicking on Analyze -> Force values. Set the Value to assign as the Mean between cursors 1..2, and region to force as Cursors 3..4`.

  6. Save this file as a new .abf file with a different name than the original file.

  7. Import the file into R using import_ABF_file().

  8. Insert the stored abf fiile into the data argument of this function.

  9. Double-check that the plot x- and y-limits are not cutting off the data.

  10. Adjust arguments like the trace_annotation and plot_colour.

  11. Try generating separate plots for both the baseline and post-hormone/treatment conditions.

  12. You can later assemble them into a full figure using p1 + p2 notation with the patchwork library.

  13. If you keep the limits and scales the same for both plots, you can hide the scale bar for one of the traces.

This function is quite similar to plot_spontaneous_current_trace(). Some of the default values for plot ranges (e.g. plot_x_min and plot_x_max) are set to automatically be within the range of the evoked current trace. IMPORTANT! Do not forget to check that your plot limits are not cutting off any part of your trace, and ensure that if you only show the scale bars for one trace, that they all use the same plot limits and scale!

See also

import_ABF_file()

Examples


plot_evoked_current_trace(
data = sample_evoked_current_trace_abf,
include_scale_bar = "yes",
k_value = 100,
include_scale_bar_label = "no",
trace_annotation = "Baseline"
)
